newsitem.title: USA: Banks ask U.S. for electronic tax report guidance.
newsitem.headline: Banks ask U.S. for electronic tax report guidance.

text.p: A leading bank trade group on Wednesday asked the Internal Revenue Service to issue detailed rules to promote the use of electronic signatures on tax documents.

With the government accepting more and more tax filings in electronic form, continued reliance on taxpayers' written signatures threatens to erode potential cost savings, the American Bankers Association said in a letter to the IRS obtained by Reuters.
Electronic signatures could "significantly reduce costs and administrative burdens," the group said in its letter, which was co-signed by the New York Clearing House.
Last December, the IRS and the Treasury Department issued regulations authorizing electronic signatures on tax returns and related documents.
But guidance issued to date has not specified the circumstances in which banks and other institutions may electronically obtain tax certification data, the bank group said.
Certain tax forms require taxpayers to provide some information and certify that the information is correct by signing the form. Many such forms require periodic recertification, the bank group said.

"U.S. financial institutions need to be given clear authority to obtain tax certification data under penalty of perjury as well as to obtain alternative electronic signatures authenticated via electronic means," the groups said.
Alternative procedures that could be treated as electronic signatures include telephone, digital and voice-autheticated measures.
